text: The 2021 tree-cover loss of approximately 81.3 hectares within the rural property (ASSET-A) is corroborated by independent Earth-observation evidence. The University of Maryland's Global Forest Change data (Hansen/UMD) detected this loss, which was also supported by the European Commission's Joint Research Centre Global Forest Cover 2020 data. The latter agreed on 98% of the event area. The Uruguay Ministry of Livestock, Agriculture and Fisheries' forest map identified the area as planted forest, primarily with Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda. However, the evidence does not specify the cause of the loss or whether it was legal or authorized.
